9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: I pushed open the large doors to the War Room and stepped inside.

11.text: I could see the pillars of smoke from the air during the flight.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: As the engine stopped, my ears were still ringing from the loud noise.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: I fixed the collar of my old army uniform, feeling comfortable in it. This whole trip reminded me of the good old days at Camp Domus.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: A soldier opened the door and led me toward a long line of his compatriots, where General Taddeus Azaro and General Carlos Azaro were both waiting for me. They were surrounded by numerous cameras.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: All of the soldiers simultaneously turned and saluted me. The sound of their boots cut through the helicopter's slowing propeller.

20.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
20.text: "I trust the skies were kind to you, Your Majesty."

21.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
21.text: "Thank you for accepting our request, my liege. Welcome to FOB Bull Charge."

22.speaker: Player_Romus
22.text: "It is a pleasure to be here. I've been wanting to see the front lines with my own eyes."

23.speaker: Player_Romus
23.text: "Skip the pleasantries, General Azaro. We have much to discuss."

24.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
24.text: "Everything will be discussed, as planned, Your Majesty."

25.speaker: Player_Romus
25.text: "I would much rather be in Porte Drazon right now. I hope this meeting is worth my time."

26.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
26.text: "I'm glad to hear it, Your Majesty."

27.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
27.text: "My daughter will be arriving after dinner. But for now..."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "I do hope that you did not put your King in danger by forcing me to come here."

30.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
30.text: "We have taken every precaution, Your Majesty. You have nothing to fear."

31.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
31.text: "This way, Your Majesty. You must be hungry after your trip. We have already prepared your quarters."

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: He was right. Pride was written all over their faces.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: The soldiers joined in and chanted the words in unison.

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "I will dine together with the soldiers in the barracks."

36.speaker: Player_Romus
36.text: "Invite this soldier to dine with us, General."

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: He gestured toward a tent. Inside, there was a lavish table piled high with an outrageous amount of food, reserved only for nobility.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: We went down the line, conducting a thorough inspection. I shook hands and saluted until I lost count.

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: After saluting, I shook hands with them. I leaned forward so only they could hear.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: He turned toward his troops and saluted them.

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: I wasn't sure if it was my imagination, but I thought I heard a gulp from the soldier standing behind me. He was a mere boy, barely out of his teens, all skin and bones.

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: "I would have preferred a tablecloth, but I suppose this is acceptable. Very well. Let's get on with it."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: We sat at the table, where the two generals gave a brief but comprehensive update on the base’s operations.

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: I tried to stomach the terrible food. It was perhaps the worst meal of my life, but I persevered.

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: Carlos nodded in assent and led me to the barracks, where dinner was just now being served. The soldiers gaped in awe as their king sat to eat with them.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: The rest of the dinner was rather uneventful. I talked about my own time in the military, getting a few laughs from the stories I told.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: The rest of the dinner was rather uneventful. I listened to a few stories from the battlefield.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: Carlos nodded his assent and gestured for the boy to enter the tent with us. He gaped in awe as he sat to eat next to his king.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: There were tears in his eyes as he tore into his meal, proclaiming it the best food he'd ever tasted in his life.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: After the meal, a soldier came by to let us know that Duchess Azaro had arrived. We moved to another tent.

54.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
54.text: "Take a look around. Morale is at its peak -- higher than it’s been in months. The men are energized, eager to have their king with them."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "Now that you're here, we can begin."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "Thank God. I was about to die from boredom. General?"

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: Cameras went off with blinding flashes.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: The military helicopter touched down on the helipad as a few medical helicopters took off and another landed.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: A soldier opened the door and saluted immediately. His eyes were blank, looking but not actually seeing. They were the eyes of someone who had seen hell.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: General Taddeus Azaro and General Carlos Azaro were both seated around a table along with a number of other high-ranking officers, arguing loudly.

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: The last man in line towered over all the others. He was at least two meters tall, with a number of scars on his face.

69.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
69.text: "This is Major Tigris. Hero of Fort Ales. He single-handedly eliminated 32 enemy combatants. A record."

70.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
70.text: "One of the best men I've ever seen in all my days in the army."

71.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
71.text: Gesture for him to kiss your ring.

72.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
72.text: Place your hand on his head and say a prayer.

73.speaker: Player_Romus
73.text: "On your feet, soldier. You bow before no one. Thank you for your service."

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: The giant knelt before me obediently.

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: This honor was granted to very few people in the military. He kissed the ring in great disbelief, then rose to his feet with a wholehearted salute.

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: He was taken aback and looked cautiously at Taddeus. After a nod of confirmation from the general, he got up and saluted me.

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: He repeated the prayer, then rose to his feet with a wholehearted salute.

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "I expect nothing less from our military. Everyone here should strive to be like him."

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: He got up on his feet and saluted wholeheartedly.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: A scream cut through his words. A soldier on a stretcher was crying out for his mother as he was moved into a medical helicopter. He was covered in bloody bandages.

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: Taddeus and Carlos continued arguing, seemingly unfazed by the scream. However, when a soldier whispered in their ear regarding my arrival, they quickly assumed a professional demeanor.

82.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
82.text: "Ah. My liege. Thank you for accepting our request. Welcome to FOB Iron Gate."

83.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
83.text: "I trust the skies were kind to you, Your Highness."

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: After saluting, I shook hands with them. I leaned forward so only they could hear.

85.speaker: Player_Romus
85.text: "I do hope that you did not put your King in danger by forcing me to come here."

86.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
86.text: "We have taken every precaution, Your Majesty. You have nothing to fear."

87.speaker: Player_Romus
87.text: "I wanted to see the frontline with my own eyes. Or whatever you call this mess."

88.speaker: Player_Romus
88.text: "Skip the pleasantries, General Azaro. We have much to discuss."

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "You couldn't put together a proper welcome party?"

92.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
92.text: "I am sorry, Your Majesty. We were in the middle of a strategic discussion."

93.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
93.text: "Duchess Azaro will be arriving shortly. But for now..."

94.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
94.text: "Take a look around. Morale is at its peak -- higher than it’s been in months. The men are energized, eager to have their king with them."

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: I cast my eye over the bedraggled group of soldiers. Most of them seemed too tired to have even registered my presence.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: Taddeus turned and saluted the soldiers.

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: A few meek shouts rose from the soldiers. Most of them continued with their duties, transporting sandbags and injured compatriots.

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: Taddeus halted two soldiers rushing to transport a wounded man on a stretcher. The soldier's height made him nearly too large for it, and his injuries left little hope -- he wouldn't last much longer.

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Taddeus held his hand and said a prayer. The man let out a final sigh. His fellow soldiers continued carrying him, slower than before.

101.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
101.text: "I remember when he first joined my battalion. He kept showing everyone photos of his daughter..."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "Don't blame yourself. This is not your fault. It is mine."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "This is entirely your fault. If only these soldiers had a better general leading them."

105.speaker: Player_Romus
105.text: "My condolences. I am sure he was an excellent soldier."

106.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
106.text: "God damn it! That was Major Tigris! One of the best men I've seen in all my days in the army."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "His death will be avenged, General Azaro. I promise."

108.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
108.text: "Forgive me, Your Majesty, but I cannot let you speak ill of yourself. My honor won't allow it."

110.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
110.text: "I told you that the left flank is no-go!"

111.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
111.text: "Nevertheless, your presence here is already helping with our situation."

112.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
112.text: "Look around at these men. They're prepared to fight for their country to their final breath."

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: He was right. They looked at me with hope in their eyes. Despite everything.

114.speaker: Player_Romus
114.text: "Sons and daughters of Rizia. Do not falter! We will be victorious! No matter what!"

115.speaker: Player_Romus
115.text: "Times may be tough. But know this, your sacrifices for our country will never be in vain."

116.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
116.text: "Thank you for your encouraging words, Your Majesty."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "Fear not. Fight for your King. Fight for your country!"

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: "We shall all return to the bosom of our God one way or another. May it be with pride and honor!"

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: The tired soldiers got up on their feet. They saluted and started chanting in weary voices.

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: A soldier came by to let us know that Duchess Azaro had arrived.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: We moved to the briefing room.

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: General Taddeus Azaro and General Carlos Azaro were there, deep in conversation with a few high-ranking officers.

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: They all turned to me and saluted.

129.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
129.text: "I just returned from the frontline today, bearing news."

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: As if on cue, the doors swung open and Lucita walked in.

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "Now that you are here, we can begin."

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: Lucita got up and gestured at the other military staff present in the tent to leave.

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: Lucita got up and gestured at the other military staff present in the tent to leave.

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: Lucita got up and gestured at the other military staff present in the room to leave.

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: Everyone was quiet as they left, leaving me with my thoughts, all alone, in the grand room.

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: The disgraced general rolled his wheelchair out. Carlos took his leave as well.

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: Everyone was quiet as they left, leaving me all alone with my thoughts in the cold tent.

225.speaker: Narrator
225.text: I wasn't sure if it was my imagination, but I thought I heard a gulp from the soldier standing behind me. He was a youngster, barely 24, all skin and bones.

226.speaker: Narrator
226.text: Her father saluted once more from his wheelchair as an aide rolled him out. Carlos took his leave as well.

228.speaker: Player_Romus
228.text: "This feels right. The two of us, fighting side by side."

236.speaker: Narrator
236.text: My war councilor and I looked at each other in silence. It was hard to read her expression.

237.speaker: Narrator
237.text: Taddeus looked back at me remorsefully as he rolled his wheelchair out. Carlos took his leave as well.

238.speaker: Narrator
238.text: My war councilor and I regarded each other in silence.

239.speaker: Player_Romus
239.text: "Give it to me straight, Luce. Are you sure we can win?"

245.speaker: Lucita Azaro
245.text: "I've never been more sure of anything else in my life."

251.speaker: Lucita Azaro
251.text: "We have it on good authority that she's being kept in Solles. We should be able to get her out soon."

252.speaker: Lucita Azaro
252.text: "The Princess is at the forefront of all of our minds. We won't rest until she's found."

256.speaker: Narrator
256.text: Her medals clinked against mine as she leaned in for a kiss.

257.speaker: Narrator
257.text: Her medals bumped against my chest as she leaned in for a kiss.

258.speaker: Narrator
258.text: She clasped her arms around my neck and whispered into my ear.

260.speaker: Lucita Azaro
260.text: "For every hair they touch on her head, I'll kill a dozen of them myself."

261.speaker: Narrator
261.text: Lucita stepped back and took a last fond look at me before running to join her father.

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "I know your father, Lucita. A show of power is the only thing a man like that understands."

269.speaker: Player_Romus
269.text: "Do you have a problem with how I handle things?"

278.speaker: Lucita Azaro
278.text: "The Princess is at the forefront of all of our minds. We won't rest until she's found."

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "I'm sorry, Luce. I don't know what came over me."

281.speaker: Lucita Azaro
281.text: "It was your right to discipline him. Two major losses in two wars against Pales is unforgivable."

282.speaker: Lucita Azaro
282.text: "But I'm begging you, Romus. Leave us Azaros to handle our own affairs. Don't bring more public disgrace to our house."

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: She squeezed my hand and shook her head sadly.

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: She took a sad last look at me before running to join her father.

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "We have to win this, Luce. I can't afford a loss."

286.speaker: Narrator
286.text: A grim look of determination spread on her face.

287.speaker: Lucita Azaro
287.text: "We'll do whatever it takes, Romus. Just trust in your military."

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: She gave my hand a quick squeeze before running out to join her father.

289.speaker: Lucita Azaro
289.text: "For every hair they touch on her head, I'll kill a dozen of them. Personally."

292.speaker: Lucita Azaro
292.text: "I'm sorry we failed you, Your Majesty."

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "Give it to me straight. How screwed are we?"

296.speaker: Lucita Azaro
296.text: "There's always hope, Your Majesty. Just trust in your military."

301.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
301.text: "He's being recommended for the Star of Valor."

303.speaker: Narrator
303.text: The Star of Valor was Rizia’s highest military honor.

304.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
304.text: "Well, if you had listened to my advice in the first place-"

305.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
305.text: "I stand with Taddeus. This is not your doing."

306.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
306.text: "I stand by Taddeus in this, Your Majesty. We are both accountable for what has transpired."
